subject: maths
description: Typed (non-OCR) maths stems written the way a student types them: clean unicode/ASCII maths, unit labels where natural, no options blocks. expectedFamily/expectedPictureClass are the honest oracle for the right picture, not a transcript of current engine behaviour. expectsDiagram:false marks stems where text-only is the honest answer. contradicts lists picture classes that would be a wrong picture for the stem (hard gate); everything else is a reported work list. Never selected by the live runtime.

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 25 like cricket, 20 like football and 10 like both. Draw a Venn diagram and find how many students like neither game.
questions.note: Two overlapping circles inside a universe rectangle; no scene family currently owns set diagrams.

questions.question: Out of 100 students, 40 read Hindi, 50 read English, 30 read Sanskrit, 15 read Hindi and English, 10 read English and Sanskrit, 8 read Hindi and Sanskrit, and 5 read all three. Draw a Venn diagram and find how many read none of the three languages.
questions.note: Three-circle Venn with the eight regions labelled from the inside out.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of the greatest integer function f(x) = [x] for -2 <= x <= 3 and mark the jump at each integer.
questions.note: Step graph with open and closed endpoint dots at each integer.

questions.question: Check whether the relation R = {(a, b) : a - b is divisible by 3} on the set of integers is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
questions.note: Property verification is symbol pushing; no honest picture.

questions.question: Given the functions f : x -> 2x + 3 and g : x -> x^2, find the compositions f o g and g o f and check whether they are equal.
questions.note: Pure algebraic composition; a diagram would be decoration.

questions.question: How many relations can be defined on a set containing 4 elements, and how many of these are reflexive?
questions.note: Counting argument; text-only is the honest answer.

questions.question: How many subsets does a set with 5 elements have, and how many of them are proper subsets?
questions.note: 2^n counting; no picture earns its place.

questions.question: Shade the region of the Argand plane given by |z - 2 + i| <= 3.
questions.note: Closed disc centred at (2, -1) with radius 3 on the complex plane.

questions.question: In the Argand plane, describe and sketch the locus of z satisfying |z - 3| = |z + 3|.
questions.note: Perpendicular bisector of the segment joining 3 and -3, i.e. the imaginary axis.

questions.question: Find the locus of the complex number z if |z - 1| = 2|z + 1|, and identify the curve in the Argand plane.
questions.note: Apollonius circle; ratio-of-distances locus is a circle, not a line.

questions.question: Sketch the set of points z in the Argand plane with arg(z - 1) = π/4.
questions.note: Open ray from (1, 0) at 45°, excluding the endpoint.

questions.question: Plot the cube roots of unity on the Argand plane and show that they form an equilateral triangle.
questions.note: Three points on the unit circle at 120° spacing joined into a triangle.

questions.question: Express z = 1 + i√3 in polar form and mark it on the Argand plane with its modulus and argument.
questions.note: Point at (1, √3) with the radius vector and the 60° argument angle marked.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of y = x^2 - 5x + 6 and use it to state where the expression is negative.
questions.note: Upward parabola with roots at 2 and 3; the sign question is read off the graph.

questions.question: Without solving, determine the nature of the roots of 3x^2 - 4x + 5 = 0.
questions.note: Discriminant arithmetic; text-only is honest.

questions.question: Form a quadratic equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 - √3.
questions.note: Sum and product of roots; no picture.

questions.question: Using determinants, find the area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 3), B(4, 5) and C(-2, 6), and plot the triangle.
questions.note: Three plotted vertices joined into a triangle on axes.

questions.question: Show that the points (2, 3), (4, 7) and (6, 11) are collinear using determinants.
questions.note: Three points falling on one drawn line makes the zero-area claim visible.

questions.question: If A = [[2, 3], [1, 4]], find the inverse of A using the adjoint method.
questions.note: Matrix arithmetic; no picture.

questions.question: Solve the system 2x + 3y = 7 and x - y = 1 using Cramer's rule.
questions.note: Determinant arithmetic; the line picture is not what is asked.

questions.question: In how many ways can a committee of 3 men and 2 women be formed from 6 men and 5 women?
questions.note: nCr product; text-only.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements of the letters of the word PERMUTATION are possible?
questions.note: Factorial with repeated letters; text-only.

questions.question: In how many ways can 8 people be seated around a circular table?
questions.note: (n-1)! counting; a table sketch adds nothing.

questions.question: Find the middle term in the expansion of (x + 2/x)^8.
questions.note: General-term formula; text-only.

questions.question: Find the coefficient of x^5 in the expansion of (1 + x)^11.
questions.note: Binomial coefficient lookup; text-only.

questions.question: Using the binomial theorem, find the remainder when 7^103 is divided by 25.
questions.note: Number-theoretic manipulation; text-only.

questions.question: The 7th term of an arithmetic progression is 20 and its 13th term is 32. Find the sum of the first 20 terms.
questions.note: Two linear equations in a and d; text-only.

questions.question: Find the sum to infinity of the geometric series 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + ...
questions.note: a/(1-r); text-only.

questions.question: Find the sum of the first n terms of the series 1 + 3x + 5x^2 + 7x^3 + ... where |x| < 1.
questions.note: Arithmetico-geometric manipulation; text-only.

questions.question: A function is defined as f(x) = x^2 for x <= 1 and f(x) = 2x - 1 for x > 1. Draw its graph and check whether it is continuous at x = 1.
questions.note: Two branch curves meeting (or not) at x = 1 is the whole argument.

questions.question: Show that f(x) = |x - 2| is continuous at x = 2 but not differentiable there, and sketch the graph.
questions.note: V-shaped graph with the corner at (2, 0).

questions.question: Discuss the continuity of f(x) = [x], the greatest integer function, at x = 2.
questions.note: Step graph showing the jump at x = 2 with open/closed dots.

questions.question: Verify Rolle's theorem for f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 on the interval [1, 3].
questions.note: Parabola with equal endpoint values and the horizontal tangent at x = 2.

questions.question: Verify the mean value theorem for f(x) = x^2 on [1, 4] and find the point where the tangent is parallel to the chord.
questions.note: Curve, chord, and the parallel tangent at x = 5/2.

questions.question: Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = x^3 - 2x + 1 at the point (1, 0).
questions.note: Cubic with attached tangent and perpendicular normal at (1, 0).

questions.question: For the curve x = t^2 and y = 2t, find the equation of the tangent at t = 1 and sketch the curve near that point.
questions.note: Parametric parabola y^2 = 4x with tangent at (1, 2); t must not be treated as x.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of y = 1/x and mark its asymptotes.
questions.note: Two hyperbola branches with both axes as asymptotes.

questions.question: Sketch the graphs of y = e^x and y = ln x on the same axes and explain how the two graphs are related.
questions.note: Mirror pair about y = x; inverse-function relationship read off the picture.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit of (sin 3x)/x as x tends to 0.
questions.note: Standard limit manipulation; text-only.

questions.question: Differentiate sqrt(x) with respect to x from first principles.
questions.note: Limit-of-difference-quotient algebra; text-only.

questions.question: If x^2 + y^2 + xy = 5, find dy/dx at the point (1, 1).
questions.note: The stem states the curve x^2+y^2+xy=5; drawing that curve is honest and helps locate (1,1). Not an invention.

questions.question: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the parabola y = x^2 and the line y = 4.
questions.note: Shaded region between curve and line, not just the two curves.

questions.question: Find the area of the region {(x, y) : x^2 <= y <= x + 2}.
questions.note: Region stated as inequalities; the picture is the shaded set between the bounds.

questions.question: Using integration, find the area of the circle x^2 + y^2 = 16.
questions.note: Circle with the quarter-disc region and a representative strip; circle_figure alone would omit the region.

questions.question: Find the area under the curve y = sin x from x = 0 to x = π.
questions.note: One arch of sine with the region beneath it shaded.

questions.question: Find the area of the region enclosed between the parabolas y^2 = 4x and x^2 = 4y.
questions.note: Lens-shaped region between the two parabolas from (0,0) to (4,4).

questions.question: Sketch the region given by |x| + |y| <= 1 and find its area.
questions.note: Square (diamond) with vertices on the axes; region stated as an inequality.

questions.question: Find the area of the smaller region bounded by the circle x^2 + y^2 = 4 and the line x + y = 2.
questions.note: Circular segment cut off by the chord from (2,0) to (0,2).

questions.question: Using integration, find the area of the triangle bounded by the lines y = 2x, y = 0 and x = 3.
questions.note: Right triangle under y = 2x from 0 to 3, shaded.

questions.question: The region bounded by y = x^2, the x-axis and x = 2 is revolved about the x-axis. Sketch the solid and find its volume.
questions.note: Generating region plus a representative disk; a bare curve is not the solid.

questions.question: Find the volume of the solid formed when the region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is rotated about the x-axis.
questions.note: Disk-method picture: region, axis of rotation, representative disk.

questions.question: Evaluate the integral of x e^x with respect to x.
questions.note: Pure indefinite integration by parts; text-only.

questions.question: Evaluate: ∫ dx / ((x - 1)(x + 2)).
questions.note: Partial fractions; text-only.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral of x / (1 + x^2) from x = 0 to x = 1.
questions.note: Substitution computation; the area picture is not asked.

questions.question: Evaluate the integral of x^2 from 0 to 2 as the limit of a sum.
questions.note: Riemann-sum algebra is the point here; text-only is honest.

questions.question: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = (1 + y^2)/(1 + x^2).
questions.note: Separate and integrate; text-only.

questions.question: Solve dy/dx + y/x = x^2 given that y = 1 when x = 1.
questions.note: Integrating-factor computation; text-only.

questions.question: Find the integrating factor of the differential equation dy/dx + 2y tan x = sin x.
questions.note: e^(∫P dx) lookup; text-only.

questions.question: Form the differential equation of the family of circles touching the x-axis at the origin, and sketch two members of the family.
questions.note: Nested circles tangent to the x-axis at O make the family visible.

questions.question: Find the order and the degree of the differential equation (d^2y/dx^2)^3 + (dy/dx)^2 + y = 0.
questions.note: Definitional readout; text-only.

questions.question: In a culture, the bacteria count doubles every 2 hours. In how many hours will it become 8 times the original count?
questions.note: Exponent comparison; text-only.

questions.question: Find the centre and the radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0, and sketch it.
questions.note: Circle centred (2, -3), radius 5, drawn on axes; implicit_conic also acceptable in spirit.

questions.question: Find the foci, the eccentricity and the lengths of the axes of the ellipse x^2/25 + y^2/9 = 1.
questions.note: Ellipse with both axes and foci marked; a 2D conic must never become a 3D frame.

questions.question: For the hyperbola x^2/9 - y^2/16 = 1, find the eccentricity, the foci and the length of the latus rectum.
questions.note: Two hyperbola branches with foci; the documented wrong pictures are a circle or a 3D frame.

questions.question: Sketch the rectangular hyperbola xy = 4 and mark its vertices.
questions.note: xy = c^2 branches in quadrants I and III with vertices (2,2) and (-2,-2).

questions.question: For the parabola y^2 = 8x, find the coordinates of the focus, the equation of the directrix and the length of the latus rectum.
questions.note: Right-opening parabola with focus (2,0) and directrix x = -2; not a function of x.

questions.question: Find the focus and the directrix of the parabola x^2 = -8y and sketch it.
questions.note: Downward-opening parabola with focus (0,-2) and directrix y = 2.

questions.question: Identify the conic 9x^2 + 4y^2 - 36x + 8y + 4 = 0 and find its centre.
questions.note: General second-degree form completing to an ellipse centred (2, -1).

questions.question: Find the angle between the lines y = 2x + 3 and y = -x + 5, and show both lines on one diagram.
questions.note: Two intersecting lines with the angle marked at their intersection.

questions.question: Find the distance of the point (3, -5) from the line 3x - 4y - 26 = 0, and show the perpendicular from the point to the line.
questions.note: Line, external point, and the foot of the perpendicular.

questions.question: Find the equations of the bisectors of the angles between the lines 3x + 4y - 7 = 0 and 12x - 5y + 8 = 0.
questions.note: Two given lines and both bisectors through the intersection point.

questions.question: The vertices of a triangle are A(2, 3), B(-4, 1) and C(6, -5). Plot the triangle and find its centroid and orthocentre.
questions.note: Plotted triangle with the two centres marked inside/outside as computed.

questions.question: Find the equation of the locus of a point that moves so that it is always equidistant from the points (2, 0) and (0, 4).
questions.note: Perpendicular bisector of the join of the two fixed points.

questions.question: Find the length of the tangent drawn from the point (10, 4) to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25, and draw the figure.
questions.note: Circle, external point, tangent segment, and the right angle at the point of contact.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the point dividing the segment joining A(1, 2) and B(7, 8) internally in the ratio 2 : 1, and mark it on the segment.
questions.note: Segment AB with the dividing point at the 2:1 position.

questions.question: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the line joining the points (2, 3) and (5, 9)?
questions.note: Negative-reciprocal arithmetic; text-only.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the lines 2x + 3y - 5 = 0, x - y + 1 = 0 and 3x + ky - 4 = 0 are concurrent.
questions.note: Solve the first two, substitute in the third; text-only.

questions.question: Find the shortest distance between the lines r = (î + ĵ) + t(2î - ĵ + k̂) and r = (2î + ĵ - k̂) + s(3î - 5ĵ + 2k̂).
questions.note: Two skew lines in one 3D frame; flattening onto a guessed 2D circle is the documented bug.

questions.question: Find the vector equation of the line passing through the point (1, 2, 3) and parallel to the vector 2i - j + 4k, and sketch it in a 3D frame.
questions.note: Space frame, the anchor point, and the line along the direction vector.

questions.question: Find the equation of the plane through the point (2, -1, 3) with normal vector 3i + 2j - k.
questions.note: Plane patch with its normal arrow at the given point.

questions.question: Find the angle between the planes 2x + y - 2z = 5 and 3x - 6y - 2z = 7.
questions.note: Two intersecting plane patches with the dihedral angle marked.

questions.question: Find the angle between the line (x - 1)/2 = (y + 1)/3 = z/6 and the plane 10x + 2y - 11z = 3.
questions.note: Line piercing the plane with the complement-of-normal angle shown.

questions.question: Find the distance of the point (3, -2, 1) from the plane 2x - y + 2z + 3 = 0.
questions.note: Point, plane patch, and the perpendicular foot.

questions.question: Find the image of the point (1, 3, 4) in the plane x - y + z = 5.
questions.note: Point, its mirror image, and the plane as the perpendicular bisector.

questions.question: Find the equation of the plane passing through the points (1, 1, 0), (1, 2, 1) and (-2, 2, -1).
questions.note: Three plotted space points spanning the plane patch.

questions.question: Show that the lines (x + 3)/3 = (y - 1)/1 = (z - 5)/5 and (x + 1)/1 = (y - 2)/2 = (z - 5)/5 are coplanar.
questions.note: Both lines drawn inside the one plane containing them.

questions.question: A line makes angles of 90°, 60° and 30° with the positive x, y and z axes. Find its direction cosines.
questions.note: Frame with the line and its three axis angles.

questions.question: Find the projection of the vector a = 2i + 3j + 2k on the vector b = i + 2j + k.
questions.note: Both vectors from one origin with the projection foot marked.

questions.question: Two vectors of magnitudes 6 and 8 act at a point with an angle of 60° between them. Draw the parallelogram of vectors and find the magnitude of the resultant.
questions.note: Parallelogram construction with the diagonal as resultant.

questions.question: Find the area of the triangle whose adjacent sides are given by the vectors a = i + 2j + 3k and b = 2i - j + k.
questions.note: Two side vectors from a shared vertex; area is half the cross-product magnitude.

questions.question: Find a unit vector perpendicular to both a = 2i + j - k and b = i - j + 2k.
questions.note: a, b, and the normalised cross product shown perpendicular to both.

questions.question: Find the volume of the parallelepiped whose coterminous edges are a = i + j, b = j + k and c = i + k, using the scalar triple product.
questions.note: A parallelepiped is a 3D figure; three edge vectors in one space frame.

questions.question: Find the angle between the vectors a = i + j - k and b = i - j + k.
questions.note: Two vectors from one origin with the included angle marked.

questions.question: Show that the points with position vectors 2i + 3j, 4i + 7j and 6i + 11j are collinear.
questions.note: Three position points falling on one drawn line.

questions.question: An aircraft flies 100 km due east and then 60 km due north. Represent the two displacements as vectors and find the magnitude and direction of the resultant displacement.
questions.note: Head-to-tail triangle with the resultant closing side.

questions.question: If a . b = 0 for two non-zero vectors a and b, what is the angle between a and b?
questions.note: One-line definitional consequence; text-only.

questions.question: Bag I contains 3 red and 4 black balls and Bag II contains 5 red and 6 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is found to be red. Draw a tree diagram and find the probability that it came from Bag I.
questions.note: Two-stage probability tree; no scene family owns tree diagrams.

questions.question: A bag has 4 red and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. Draw the probability tree and find the probability that both are red.
questions.note: Two-level tree with branch probabilities 4/10 then 3/9.

questions.question: If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2, draw a Venn diagram and find P(A ∪ B) and P(A' ∩ B).
questions.note: Two overlapping event circles with the three region probabilities.

questions.question: Find the mean and the standard deviation of the observations 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
questions.note: Formula evaluation; text-only.

questions.question: Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is 8 given that the first die shows 3.
questions.note: Conditional probability by counting; text-only.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 6 times. Find the probability of getting exactly 4 heads.
questions.note: Binomial formula; text-only.

questions.question: A random variable X takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities k, 2k, 3k and 4k. Find k and the mean of X.
questions.note: Probabilities sum to 1; text-only.

questions.question: Find the mean deviation about the mean for the data 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 17.
questions.note: Tabular computation; text-only.

questions.question: In 5 independent Bernoulli trials with success probability 1/3, find the probability of at least one success.
questions.note: Complement rule; text-only.

questions.question: From a point on the ground 40 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. Draw the figure and find the height of the tower.
questions.note: Right triangle: ground line, vertical tower, elevation angle at the observer.

questions.question: From the top of a 60 m high building, the angles of depression of the top and the bottom of a tower are 30° and 60°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.note: Two right triangles sharing the horizontal sight line from the building top.

questions.question: Draw the graph of y = sin x for 0 <= x <= 2π and mark the maximum and minimum points.
questions.note: One full period with extrema at π/2 and 3π/2.

questions.question: On the same axes, sketch y = sin x and y = sin 2x for 0 <= x <= π and mark where the two graphs intersect.
questions.note: Both curves on shared axes with the intersection points marked.

questions.question: Mark the angle 210° on a unit circle and find the values of sin 210° and cos 210°.
questions.note: Unit circle with the third-quadrant terminal arm and the reference angle.

questions.question: Find the principal value of sin⁻¹(-1/2) + cos⁻¹(-1/2).
questions.note: Principal-value lookup; text-only.

questions.question: Solve the equation 2 cos^2 x + 3 sin x = 0 and write the general solution.
questions.note: Quadratic in sin x; text-only.

questions.question: Prove that (sin 3x + sin x) / (cos 3x - cos x) = -cot x.
questions.note: Sum-to-product identity manipulation; text-only.

questions.question: Find the maximum and minimum values of 3 sin x + 4 cos x.
questions.note: R-form amplitude bound; text-only.

questions.question: Maximise Z = 3x + 4y subject to the constraints x + y <= 4, x >= 0, y >= 0. Draw the feasible region and find the corner point where Z is maximum.
questions.note: Shaded feasible triangle with corner points; the answer lives at a vertex.

questions.question: Minimise Z = 200x + 500y subject to x + 2y >= 10, 3x + 4y <= 24, x >= 0, y >= 0. Solve the problem graphically.
questions.note: Feasible quadrilateral between the two lines in the first quadrant.

questions.question: A diet needs at least 80 units of vitamin A and 100 units of minerals. Food F1 gives 3 units of vitamin A and 4 units of minerals per kg and costs ₹50 per kg; food F2 gives 6 and 3 units and costs ₹70 per kg. Formulate the linear programming problem and shade the feasible region.
questions.note: Unbounded feasible region above both constraint lines.

questions.question: Prove by mathematical induction that 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n = n(n + 1)/2 for every natural number n.
questions.note: Base case plus inductive step; text-only.

questions.question: Write the contrapositive and the converse of the statement: if a number is divisible by 9, then it is divisible by 3.
questions.note: Statement manipulation; text-only.
